fact: MOZIX, the Mozambique Internet Exchange in Maputo run by CIUEM at Eduardo Mondlane University, says it was created in May 2002 and has grown from 5 to 18 peers that exchange traffic between themselves; the site carries no date, so as_of is the 2026-08-08 capture date.

Internet Society Pulse lists MOZIX (Mozambique Internet Exchange) in its IXP tracker, from PeeringDB data as of July 2026, with 143 Gbps cumulative member port capacity (capacity, not measured traffic) and no members joined or left.
Capacity Media reports MOZIX, run by CIUEM, is Mozambique's sole IXP with 19 active peering members, and opened a new point of presence at Digital Realty's MPM1 data centre in Maputo.
Traffic: over 150 Gbps (peak) at MOZIX on 2025-05-15, with 19 peering members, as stated by CIUEM's director; the article gives no separate measurement date, so the publication date is used.

O.Economico reports the university's rector saying UEM runs the national traffic exchange point MOZIX, which lets part of the traffic between national networks be exchanged locally without crossing international infrastructure.

Diario Economico quotes the communications minister calling MozIX (Mozambique Internet Exchange Point) the national internet traffic exchange point, which the new UEM data centre will help keep running.
Internet Society Pulse's IXP Tracker lists 1 active exchange point in Mozambique with 18 members as of November 2026.
CIUEM's director says the Mozambique Internet Exchange (MozIX) has capacity of a little over 150 Gbps and 19 members peering, and iColo says it is the first and only IXP in Mozambique.
The African IXP Association's undated list of exchange points, retrieved 2026-11-09, names for Mozambique: MOZIX, Maputo.
Internet Society's report counts one IXP in Mozambique, with 37.93% of local networks connected to it.
